Incompetent

in-KOM-pih-tent — starts with 'in-' (not); an incompetent worker is simply not competent. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incompetent is lacking the skill or ability needed to do something properly.

The new intern was so incompetent at filing paperwork that half the folders ended up in the wrong drawers.

Worked Example

A plumber is hired to fix a leaky pipe but ends up flooding the entire kitchen, then leaves without cleaning up or explaining what went wrong.

Being unable to properly perform even a basic task, and making things worse instead, is exactly what it means to be incompetent. Unlike 'unlucky,' which implies bad fortune, incompetent means genuinely lacking the necessary skill.

How Incompetent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inept

inept: lacking skill; clumsy or incapable

unqualified

unqualified: not having the necessary skill or qualifications

incapable

incapable: not able to do something

Antonyms

competent

competent: having the necessary skill or ability

skilled

skilled: having ability or expertise gained through training

How Strong Is It? — unpolished → incompetent → inept

unpolished vs. incompetent

unpolished vs. incompetent: Unpolished is weaker than incompetent — someone unpolished just needs more practice, while incompetent means genuinely lacking the ability to do the job at all.

inept vs. incompetent

inept vs. incompetent: Inept can feel even sharper than incompetent in tone: both describe a lack of skill, but inept often carries a stronger note of clumsiness or embarrassment.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

prefix — com-

prefix — com-: together (Latin)

root — -pet-

root — -pet-: to seek, to aim at (Latin)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: adjective-forming (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin competere combined com- (together) with petere (to seek, to aim at) to mean 'to be fit, to coincide.' Adding in- (not) gives incompetent: someone who does not have what it takes to properly aim at and reach the goal.
